content: Waterborne diseases are caused by pathogenic microorganisms that are directly transmitted when contaminated drinking water is consumed. Contaminated water used in food preparation can also serve as a source of foodborne diseases, as the same microorganisms may be ingested through the consumption of such food. It is estimated that approximately 8 million people are affected by waterborne diseases annually. Of this burden, 88% is attributed to unsafe water supply, poor sanitation, and inadequate hygiene practices. This issue predominantly affects children in developing countries, where access to clean water and proper sanitation is limited. Waterborne diseases can be caused by a variety of pathogens, including protozoa, viruses, bacteria, and intestinal parasites.
